Back Irish oversight bodies gained new skills to supervise Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems from equality perspectives

The Council of Europe and the Department of Enterprise, Tourism and Employment of Ireland, in collaboration with the Irish AI Office and the Irish Human Rights and Equality Commission (IHREC), organised a hybrid training course on AI and anti-discrimination from 24 August to 5 November 2026. The course helped public officials understand how AI systems can affect equality and human rights, and how discrimination risks can be identified and addressed.

The course brought together Irish equality bodies, Ombuds institutions and other supervisory bodies to explore the opportunities and challenges of using AI in public and private services. Through training modules and practical case studies, participants learnt about the policy and legal frameworks on AI and what safeguards can help prevent discriminatory outcomes.

“This course created valuable opportunities for Irish officials protecting fundamental rights to acquire necessary skills to supervise AI deployment and use, particularly in respect of identifying risks of discrimination against structurally vulnerable groups, and to promote safer and more trustworthy AI systems,” said Rebecca Keatinge, IHREC. “Many thanks to the Council of Europe team for sharing their expertise and delivering this course, and to the Department and the newly established AI Office for supporting its delivery,” she continued.

The course forms part of the Council of Europe’s work to support public authorities and equality bodies in addressing the equality implications of AI. Its first delivery in Ireland marks a new step in that work, building knowledge and practical capacity among those assigned to supervise AI systems from fundamental rights, including equality, perspectives.
